sourceAuthority.operatorName: Centre de Données astronomiques de Strasbourg

providers.name: SIMBAD Astronomical Database
operations: bounded ICRS cone query over SIMBAD basic objects

analyses.inputRows: 1-500 strict astrometric measurement rows with exact source-content SHA-256
analyses.uncertainty: SIMBAD-style proper-motion error ellipse covariance plus first-order delta propagation and normal 95% intervals

analyses.inputRows: 5-2000 strict irregular time-series rows with explicit astronomical time system, nullable values/errors, use flags, and exact source-content SHA-256
analyses.method: weighted floating-mean generalized Lomb-Scargle least-squares sinusoid over an inclusive linear frequency grid
analyses.uncertainty: inverse-variance weighting when explicitly resolved as weighted; missing errors are preserved and never imputed

limitations: SIMBAD is an astronomical object database, not a general catalogue or complete survey; absence from a cone result is not evidence that no object exists.
Only the fixed basic-object ten-column projection is exposed. Arbitrary ADQL, uploads, async jobs, joins, provider pagination, and alternate endpoints are not accepted.
The cone is ICRS in decimal degrees and is bounded to 10 degrees and 500 objects per request.
JSON, CSV, and TSV normalize to the same canonical object projection. Null and empty optional provider values remain null and are never imputed.
The exact successful HTTP response bytes are hashed but are not embedded in the normalized result.

The kinematics analysis does not fetch missing uncertainties. It accepts explicit uncertainty fields, preserves absent values as null, and excludes incomplete rows from inference rather than imputing them.

Distance is the naive inverse of a positive parallax, not a Bayesian distance estimate. First-order delta uncertainties are withheld from inference when declared fractional-error thresholds are exceeded.
The proper-motion error ellipse supplies component covariance, but parallax-proper-motion covariance is unavailable and is explicitly assumed to be zero.
The publication figure is a deterministic Vega-Lite payload; this plugin does not bundle or claim a renderer/export runtime.
The period analysis is a single-sinusoid weighted floating-mean generalized Lomb-Scargle grid search. Reported peaks are local maxima on the declared finite grid, not detection probabilities.

No false-alarm probability, multiple-testing correction, period confidence interval, red-noise model, detrending, multi-harmonic fit, or transit model is computed. Sampling-window and cadence warnings must be reviewed independently.
Astronomical time systems are preserved exactly as declared by the caller and are not converted. BJD, HJD, JD, MJD, UTC, and TDB must not be treated as interchangeable.
No renderer is bundled. The host may render the normalized rows in its existing table or sky-coordinate surfaces without implying survey completeness.
